skills.name: Transport development in Cameroon: routes and nodes

note.text: Cameroon’s transport system combines roads, rail and water or air connections. A node’s role depends on links, terminals and its surrounding activities. Camrail identifies Douala–Yaoundé and Yaoundé–Ngaoundéré rail connections. The schematic selects these links and a Douala–Kribi road connection; it is incomplete and not to scale. It gives no timetable, condition or current travel guarantee.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to read selected Cameroon transport links without inventing missing connections. Builds on: road and rail networks. Leads to: access inequalities and multimodal planning.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Cameroon’s transport system combines roads, rail and water or air connections. A node’s role depends on links, terminals and its surrounding activities. Camrail identifies Douala–Yaoundé and Yaoundé–Ngaoundéré rail connections. The schematic selects these links and a Douala–Kribi road connection; it is incomplete and not to scale. It gives no timetable, condition or current travel guarantee.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: The diagram distinguishes selected rail links from a road link and identifies Douala and Kribi as port nodes. It does not draw a rail connection to every port. A producer beyond these lines still needs access to a terminal. Actual travel planning requires current route, service and safety information beyond a classroom schematic.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Read the legend before tracing a link. State what the drawing includes and what it cannot prove. Explain how a node could connect flows, then ask about local access, handling and service reliability.
